newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia group urges more study of nuclear bill.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia group urges more study of nuclear bill.

text.p: A leading Indonesian environment group urged parliament on Monday to study further a nuclear energy bill which it said was set to legitimise the country's first nuclear power plant.

Emmy Hafild, executive director of the Indonesian Environment Network (Walhi), told a news conference that the bill, scheduled to become law on December 12, had been discussed by a special parliamentary committee for only five full days last week.
"The discussion of the bill has been forced through so the law will be very weak," Hafild said.
The government says the bill is to update existing regulations on the use of nuclear substances and provide a framework for Indonesia's proposed nuclear power stations.
Hafild said the bill did not meet the requirements of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

Walhi says it believes the nuclear energy bill has not properly addressed the issue of the disposal of nuclear waste and the process by which any nuclear power plant will be approved by the government.
"This law is to confirm the nuclear power project that will soon start. We ask the parliament to review again the bill or delay its passing into law," Hafild said.

Discussion of the bill had been set to go ahead until November 15, but legislators said the period had been cut short after Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie was unable to attend after his wife fell ill.
Habibie has been pushing for the country's first nuclear power plant to be built in central Java starting in 1998 or 1999, pending the results of a study on the project.
